- name: int_jira__field_history_scd
      description: Slowly changing daily snapshots of Jira issue fields with forward-filled values
      grain: One row per issue_day_id (issue per day)
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_jira__pivot_daily_field_history (valid_starting_on, issue_id, issue_day_id, status, sprint, story_points, story_point_estimate)
      business_logic: 'Build a daily slowly changing snapshot from the pivoted field history: - Use all rows from intermediate.int_jira__pivot_daily_field_history. - For each issue_id, sort records by valid_starting_on ascending. - For each field in [status → status_id, sprint, story_points, story_point_estimate]: - Define update groups by maintaining a running count that increases by 1 on days when the field is non-NULL; on NULL days the count does not change. Each group starts on a non-NULL day and spans until (but not including) the next non-NULL day. - For every day within an update group, set the field’s value to the value from the first day of that group, carrying it forward across subsequent days. - Days before the first non-NULL remain NULL; later NULLs in the source are treated as no change and the prior value persists. - Output valid_starting_on, issue_id, issue_day_id, and the forward-filled fields, with status renamed to status_id. - No deduplication or final ordering is applied; the model assumes at most one row per (issue_id, valid_starting_on). Values are not transformed beyond forward-fill.'
      columns:
      - name: valid_starting_on
        data_type: DATE
        description: Snapshot date that orders updates and forward-fill
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue identifier used to group and forward-fill field histories
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_day_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique key for the daily snapshot of an issue
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: status_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Forward-filled daily status (renamed from status); NULL until first non-NULL; later NULLs treated as no change
      - name: sprint
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Forward-filled daily sprint; NULL until first non-NULL; later NULLs treated as no change
      - name: story_points

- name: int_jira__issue_calendar_spine
      description: Daily calendar spine of Jira issues with open-state window and derived week metrics
      grain: One row per issue_id per date_day
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__issue (issue_id, created_at, resolved_at)
      - intermediate.int_jira__field_history_scd (issue_id, valid_starting_on)
      business_logic: '- Build a daily date spine from 2016-01-01 through seven days after today. - For each issue, derive created_on as the calendar date of created_at. Set open_until to today if the issue is unresolved; otherwise to the calendar date of the field-history valid_starting_on. - Join issues to the date spine and include a row when date_day is on or after created_on and on or before one month after open_until. If multiple history records match, earliest_open_until_date is the minimum open_until for that issue_id and date_day. - Create issue_day_id as an MD5 hash of date_day and issue_id concatenated with no delimiter. - Derive earliest_open_until_week as the Monday start of the week containing earliest_open_until_date. - Limit the final output to date_day not later than today. - Determinism and null policy: - All timestamps are converted to calendar dates; comparisons are inclusive. - Only (issue_id, date_day) pairs that meet the window are emitted; earliest_open_until_date is non-null for all rows. - Grouping enforces one row per (issue_id, date_day); issue_day_id is unique.'
      columns:
      - name: date_day
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar date in scope (2016-01-01 through today, inclusive) when the issue is within its open window
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Jira issue identifier associated with the date_day
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_day_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: MD5 of date_day and issue_id concatenated with no delimiter; unique per (date_day, issue_id)
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: earliest_open_until_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Minimum open_until among matched history rows for this (issue_id, date_day); open_until is today if unresolved, else the field-history starting date
      - name: earliest_open_until_week
        data_type: DATE
        description: Monday week start derived from earliest_open_until_date

- name: int_jira__issue_comments
      description: Aggregates Jira comments per issue into a comment count and a newline-separated conversation string.
      grain: One row per issue_id with at least one comment whose author_user_id matches a user in staging.stg_jira__user
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__comment
      - staging.stg_jira__user
      business_logic: '- Read all rows from staging.stg_jira__comment; an initial sort by issue_id and created_at is applied in the source CTE but no ordering is enforced in the final aggregation. - Inner join to staging.stg_jira__user on author_user_id = user_id; comments without a matching user are excluded. - Group by issue_id and compute: - count_comments: count of non-NULL comment_id across the joined comments; duplicates are counted. - conversation: for each joined comment, create a line "<created_at as text> - <user_display_name>: <body>" and concatenate all lines using a single LF (newline) between lines; if any component needed for a line is NULL, that line is omitted; if all lines are omitted, the result is NULL; original casing and spacing are preserved; no trimming or normalization is applied. - Ordering: no explicit ordering is applied in the concatenation; the order of lines in the conversation is not guaranteed and may vary. - Only issue_id values with at least one joined comment appear in the output.'
      columns:
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue identifier; one row per issue_id with at least one joined comment.
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: count_comments
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of joined comments per issue; counts non-NULL comment_id and excludes comments without a matching user.
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: conversation
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Newline-separated concatenation of lines formatted as ''<created_at as text> - <user_display_name>: <body>''; line order is not guaranteed; lines with any NULL component are omitted; casing and spacing are preserved.'

- name: int_jira__issue_epic
      description: Latest Epic Link per issue based on field history (one row per issue_id with an Epic Link record)
      grain: One row per issue_id with at least one Epic Link history record
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_field_history
      business_logic: '- From intermediate.int_jira__issue_field_history, keep rows where the field_name, compared case-insensitively, starts with "epic" and ends with "link". - For each issue_id, sort the remaining rows by updated_at descending and select the single most recent record; if multiple records share the same updated_at, which one is chosen is unspecified. - Output issue_id and epic_issue_id, where epic_issue_id is the field_value of the selected record treated as text. - Exclude issues without any matching Epic Link history; if the selected field_value is null, epic_issue_id is null and the row is kept.'
      columns:
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue identifier; exactly one row per issue_id in the result
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: epic_issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR

- name: int_jira__issue_join
      description: Denormalized issue-level view joining project, status, resolution, priority, sprint, assignments, versions, and comments with select derived fields.
      grain: One row per issue_id
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_users
      - staging.stg_jira__project
      - staging.stg_jira__status
      - staging.stg_jira__status_category
      - staging.stg_jira__resolution
      - staging.stg_jira__priority
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_sprint
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_comments
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_assign_resolution
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_versions
      business_logic: '- Start from intermediate.int_jira__issue_users; include all columns unchanged. Intended grain is one row per issue_id. - Left join project using project_id to add project_name. - Left join status using status_id to add the current status name. - Left join status_category by comparing status.status_category_id and status_category.status_category_id as strings to add the status category name. - Left join resolution using resolution_id to add resolution_name. - Left join priority using priority_id to add priority_name. - Left join int_jira__issue_assign_resolution using issue_id to add first_assigned_at, last_assigned_at, and first_resolved_at. - Left join int_jira__issue_versions using issue_id to add fixes_versions and affects_versions (passed through from upstream). - Left join int_jira__issue_sprint using issue_id to add current_sprint_id, current_sprint_name, sprint_started_at, sprint_ended_at, sprint_completed_at, and count_sprint_changes (nulls become 0). - Derive is_active_sprint: true when sprint_started_at is present and in the past or now, and sprint_completed_at is missing or in the future or now; otherwise false. sprint_ended_at is not considered. Evaluation uses the warehouse current timestamp at query time. - Left join int_jira__issue_comments using issue_id to add conversation and count_comments (nulls become 0). - All joins are left joins. If any joined source has multiple rows per issue_id, the result will fan out because no de-duplication or aggregation is performed here.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_jira__issue_lifecycle_analysis
      description: Issue lifecycle metrics and activity-based classifications derived from non-null field history changes
      grain: One row per issue_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__issue
      - staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history
      business_logic: '- Build issue_activity_history from staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history: - Keep only records where field_value is present. - For each issue_id, sort changes by updated_at ascending and derive: - previous_change_time: the timestamp of the immediately prior change for the same issue; null for the first change. - change_sequence: the 1-based position of the change in the sorted list. - total_changes: the total number of non-null field_value changes for the issue (reference only). - If multiple changes share an identical updated_at within an issue, their tie-order is implementation-dependent (no secondary tiebreaker). - Build activity_patterns by retaining only changes with a previous_change_time and compute: - days_between_changes: elapsed time in days between change_time and previous_change_time. - hours_between_changes: elapsed time in hours between change_time and previous_change_time (intermediate only; not output). - Summarize per issue_id (issue_activity_summary): - total_field_changes: the count of retained changes (number of consecutive intervals). - avg_days_between_changes: average of days_between_changes. - max_days_between_changes: maximum of days_between_changes. - activity_variance: standard deviation of days_between_changes. - first_change_time: earliest change_time among retained changes. - last_change_time: latest change_time among retained changes. - When no retained changes exist, the summary has no row; downstream metrics remain null, with total_field_changes set to 0 in the final step. - Build issue_base_info from staging.stg_jira__issue and compute: - total_lifecycle_days: elapsed time in days from created_at to resolved_at; if unresolved, to the current timestamp at execution. - Final integration and classifications (left join summary to base on issue_id): - total_field_changes: set to 0 when summary is missing; other summary metrics remain null when missing. - activity_pattern: - If total_field_changes = 0 → "No Activity". - Otherwise by avg_days_between_changes: ≤1 → "High Activity"; ≤7 → "Regular Activity"; ≤30 → "Low Activity"; else → "Minimal Activity". - lifecycle_speed: - By total_lifecycle_days: ≤7 → "Fast"; ≤30 → "Normal"; ≤90 → "Slow"; else → "Very Slow". - risk_indicator (applied in order): - If total_lifecycle_days > 90 and total_field_changes < 5 → "Stagnant". - Else if max_days_between_changes > 30 → "Inactive Periods". - Else if total_field_changes > 50 → "Over Worked". - Else → "Normal". - Output one row per issue_id from staging.stg_jira__issue; the final result is ordered by issue_id ascending.'
      columns:
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Primary grouping key from Jira; exactly one output row per issue_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: issue_key
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Human-readable Jira issue key (e.g., PROJ-123)
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_type_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue type identifier from Jira
      - name: priority_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Priority identifier from Jira
      - name: project_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Project identifier from Jira
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Issue creation timestamp from Jira
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: resolved_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Issue resolution timestamp; null if unresolved
      - name: assignee_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Current assignee user identifier from Jira
      - name: reporter_user_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Reporter user identifier from Jira
      - name: total_lifecycle_days
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Fractional days from created_at to resolved_at; if unresolved, to current_timestamp at execution; no rounding
      - name: total_field_changes
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of consecutive change intervals (rows with non-null previous_change_time) over non-null field_value changes; 0 when none
      - name: avg_days_between_changes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Average of days_between_changes across change intervals; unit: days; null when no intervals'
      - name: max_days_between_changes
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Maximum of days_between_changes across change intervals; unit: days; null when no intervals'
      - name: activity_variance
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Standard deviation of days_between_changes across change intervals; null when no intervals
      - name: first_change_time
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Earliest change_time among intervals (second or later change); null when no intervals
      - name: last_change_time
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Latest change_time among intervals; null when no intervals
      - name: activity_pattern
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Classification: No Activity if total_field_changes=0; else High/Regular/Low/Minimal based on avg_days_between_changes thresholds'
        tests:
        - activity_pattern IN ('No Activity', 'High Activity', 'Regular Activity', 'Low Activity', 'Minimal Activity')
      - name: lifecycle_speed
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Classification from total_lifecycle_days: Fast (≤7), Normal (≤30), Slow (≤90), else Very Slow'
        tests:
        - lifecycle_speed IN ('Fast', 'Normal', 'Slow', 'Very Slow')
      - name: risk_indicator
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Risk classification applied in order: Stagnant, then Inactive Periods, then Over Worked, else Normal'
        tests:
        - risk_indicator IN ('Normal', 'Stagnant', 'Inactive Periods', 'Over Worked')

output.equality_policy: exact CAST AS VARCHAR per row; no trim/case/numeric/date normalization; both NULL ignored; at least one nonnull equal row; one-sided NULL differs

alternatives.expression_sql: CASE WHEN COALESCE(s.total_field_changes, 0) = 0 THEN 'No Activity' WHEN s.avg_days_between_changes <= 1 THEN 'High Activity' WHEN s.avg_days_between_changes <= 7 THEN 'Regular Activity' WHEN s.avg_days_between_changes <= 30 THEN 'Low Activity' ELSE 'Minimal Activity' END
CASE WHEN b.total_lifecycle_days <= 7 THEN 'Fast' WHEN b.total_lifecycle_days <= 30 THEN 'Normal' WHEN b.total_lifecycle_days <= 90 THEN 'Slow' ELSE 'Very Slow' END

CASE WHEN b.total_lifecycle_days > 90 AND COALESCE(s.total_field_changes, 0) < 5 THEN 'Stagnant' WHEN s.max_days_between_changes > 30 THEN 'Inactive Periods' WHEN s.total_field_changes > 50 THEN 'Over Worked' ELSE 'Normal' END

runtime_hits.line_text: with h as (select issue_id,updated_at change_time,lag(updated_at) over(partition by issue_id order by updated_at) previous_change_time from staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history where field_value is not null), a as (select issue_id,epoch(change_time-previous_change_time)/86400.0 days_between_changes from h where previous_change_time is not null), s as (select issue_id,count(*) total_field_changes,avg(days_between_changes) avg_days_between_changes,max(days_between_changes) max_days_between_changes,stddev_samp(days_between_changes) activity_variance,min(change_time) first_change_time,max(change_time) last_change_time from (select h.issue_id,h.change_time,a.days_between_changes from h join a using(issue_id) where h.previous_change_time is not null) q group by issue_id), b as (select *,epoch(coalesce(resolved_at,current_timestamp)-created_at)/86400.0 total_lifecycle_days from staging.stg_jira__issue) select b.issue_id,b.issue_key,b.issue_type_id,b.priority_id,b.project_id,b.created_at,b.resolved_at,b.assignee_user_id,b.reporter_user_id,b.total_lifecycle_days,coalesce(s.total_field_changes,0) total_field_changes,s.avg_days_between_changes,s.max_days_between_changes,s.activity_variance,s.first_change_time,s.last_change_time,case when coalesce(s.total_field_changes,0)=0 then 'No Activity' when s.avg_days_between_changes<=1 then 'High Activity' when s.avg_days_between_changes<=7 then 'Regular Activity' when s.avg_days_between_changes<=30 then 'Low Activity' else 'Minimal Activity' end activity_pattern,case when b.total_lifecycle_days<=7 then 'Fast' when b.total_lifecycle_days<=30 then 'Normal' when b.total_lifecycle_days<=90 then 'Slow' else 'Very Slow' end lifecycle_speed,case when b.total_lifecycle_days>90 and coalesce(s.total_field_changes,0)<5 then 'Stagnant' when s.max_days_between_changes>30 then 'Inactive Periods' when s.total_field_changes>50 then 'Over Worked' else 'Normal' end risk_indicator from b left join s using(issue_id)

      grain: One row per stg_jira__issue_multiselect_history row that successfully joins to stg_jira__field on field_id (duplicates preserved)

- name: int_jira__issue_sprint
      description: Synthetic issue-to-sprint mapping using a deterministic hash-based assignment; about one-third of issues are included.
      grain: One row per issue whose deterministic hash of issue_id has remainder 0 when divided by 3.
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__issue
      - staging.stg_jira__sprint
      business_logic: '- Build sprint_data from staging.stg_jira__sprint with fields (sprint_id, sprint_name, board_id, started_at, ended_at, completed_at) and assign sprint_sequence by ordering sprints ascending by started_at; ties and NULL ordering follow the database default. - Build issue_base from staging.stg_jira__issue with fields (issue_id, issue_key, created_at, resolved_at, project_id) and compute assigned_sprint_sequence by: taking a deterministic hash of issue_id, taking the remainder when divided by the number of sprints, converting to a non-negative value, then adding 1 to map to the 1-based sprint_sequence. At least one sprint is required; if there are no sprints, this model will error. - Join issues to sprints on assigned_sprint_sequence = sprint_sequence (left join). When at least one sprint exists, each included issue maps to exactly one sprint; sprint attributes reflect the matched sprint and may be NULL only if the source sprint fields are NULL. - Filter to include only issues where the deterministic hash of issue_id yields a remainder of 0 when divided by 3; issues with NULL issue_id are excluded by this filter. This selects roughly one-third of issues and is deterministic for a given issue_id and sprint set. - Output selected issue and sprint fields and set count_sprint_changes to 1 for all rows (no history modeled). Assignments depend on the set of sprints and their ordering by started_at; changes to sprint count or ordering will change assignments.'
      columns:
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Issue identifier; row included only when the hash-based 3-way filter selects it; NULL issue_id are excluded.
      - name: issue_key
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Human-readable issue key from the issue source.
      - name: created_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Issue creation timestamp from the issue source; may be NULL.
      - name: resolved_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Issue resolution timestamp from the issue source; may be NULL.
      - name: project_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Project identifier from the issue source; may be NULL.
      - name: current_sprint_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Identifier of the assigned sprint determined by the sequence mapping; NULL only if the source sprint field is NULL.
      - name: current_sprint_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Name of the assigned sprint; NULL only if the source sprint field is NULL.
      - name: board_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Board identifier of the assigned sprint; NULL only if the source sprint field is NULL.
      - name: sprint_started_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Start timestamp of the assigned sprint (used for sprint ordering); may be NULL.
      - name: sprint_ended_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: End timestamp of the assigned sprint; may be NULL.
      - name: sprint_completed_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        description: Completion timestamp of the assigned sprint; may be NULL.
      - name: count_sprint_changes
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Always 1 to represent a single synthetic assignment without history.

- name: int_jira__issue_type_parents
      description: Issues enriched with type name, revised parent linkage, and parent issue details
      grain: One row per issue_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__issue
      - staging.stg_jira__issue_type
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_epic
      business_logic: '- Start with all issues from staging.stg_jira__issue (one row per issue_id; no aggregation or ordering). - Left join intermediate.int_jira__issue_epic on issue_id to bring in epic linkage. - Set revised_parent_issue_id by using parent_issue_id when present; otherwise use epic_issue_id; treat identifiers as text; set to NULL when neither exists. - Left join staging.stg_jira__issue_type on issue_type_id to add issue_type (the type name); keep issues even when no type is found. - Left self-join using revised_parent_issue_id matched to issue_id (compared as text) to add parent_issue_type, parent_issue_name, and parent_issue_key. - Set is_parent_epic to true when the joined parent issue type equals "Epic" ignoring case; otherwise false, including when no parent exists. - All other fields are direct pass-through from staging.stg_jira__issue without transformation.'

      description: Issue records from int_jira__issue_type_parents enriched with assignee and reporter attributes; parent_issue_id is derived from revised_parent_issue_id or parent_issue_id
      grain: One row per issue; may produce multiple rows per issue if the user table has duplicate user_id entries
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_type_parents
      - staging.stg_jira__user
      business_logic: '- Start with all columns from intermediate.int_jira__issue_type_parents. - Derive parent_issue_id by taking revised_parent_issue_id when present; otherwise use the original parent_issue_id; both are treated as text, and the result is null if both are missing. - Keep all source columns unchanged; because issue_id is also selected explicitly, the output includes duplicate source versions named issue_id_1 and parent_issue_id_1. - Join the user table twice using left joins: on assignee_user_id to add assignee_name, assignee_timezone, assignee_email; on reporter_user_id to add reporter_email, reporter_name, reporter_timezone. - No filters, aggregation, or ordering are applied. All issues are retained; unmatched users yield null attributes. If the user table has multiple rows for a user_id, the result may have multiple rows per issue (no de-duplication).'

      - name: parent_issue_id

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_jira__issue_versions
      description: Aggregates the most recent affected and fix version names per issue into comma-separated strings.
      grain: One row per issue_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__version
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_multiselect_history
      business_logic: '- Filter issue multiselect history to records where field_id is ''versions'' or ''fixVersions''. - For each (issue_id, field_id), identify the most recent updated_at; if multiple rows share the most recent timestamp, keep all of them. - Convert field_value to an integer version_id and join to the version table to retrieve version_name; only matching version_ids contribute. - For each (issue_id, field_id), concatenate version_name values into a single string using ", ": - No specific ordering is applied. - Duplicates are kept. - NULL names are ignored; if none remain, the result is NULL. - Map the concatenated string to: - affects_versions when field_id = ''versions'' - fixes_versions when field_id = ''fixVersions'' - Produce a single row per issue_id by carrying forward the non-null value for each version column.'
      columns:
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique Jira issue identifier
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: affects_versions
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated version_name list from the most recent 'versions' update; no ordering; duplicates kept; NULL names ignored; NULL if none
      - name: fixes_versions
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Comma-separated version_name list from the most recent 'fixVersions' update; no ordering; duplicates kept; NULL names ignored; NULL if none

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_jira__pivot_daily_field_history
      description: Daily pivot of latest status, sprint, story points, and story point estimate per issue on days with changes
      grain: One row per issue_id per valid_starting_on (only days with a change in any pivoted field)
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_field_history
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_multiselect_history
      business_logic: '- Read single-value field changes from intermediate.int_jira__issue_field_history and multiselect field changes from intermediate.int_jira__issue_multiselect_history. - For multiselect changes, aggregate all values per (field_id, field_name, issue_id, updated_at) into one string joined by ", "; duplicates are preserved; NULL inputs are excluded; no ordering is enforced in the concatenation. - Union the aggregated multiselect changes with the single-value changes. - For each issue and field, each change timestamp starts a validity period that lasts until the next change; also derive the calendar date of the start. - Keep only relevant fields: status by field_id (case-insensitive), and sprint, story points, story point estimate by field_name (case-insensitive). - For each issue, field, and calendar date, retain the last change of that day (the highest change timestamp for that day; no tie-breaker beyond timestamp). - Replace a NULL field value with the literal "is_null"; otherwise keep the original text (including any comma-joined multiselect values). - Pivot to columns: status from field_id; sprint, story points, and story point estimate from field_name. Group by issue and date, and carry the week-start of the selected change timestamp. Use max as a pass-through since there is at most one selected value per field per day. - Output includes only dates where at least one relevant field changed for the issue. Unchanged fields on that date remain NULL; fields changed to true NULL appear as "is_null". - Compute issue_day_id as the MD5 of valid_starting_on concatenated with issue_id, with no delimiter.'
      columns:
      - name: valid_starting_on
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar date on which the day's selected field updates became valid
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: issue_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Jira issue identifier for the daily pivot row
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: valid_starting_at_week
        data_type: DATE
        description: Week start date based on the selected change timestamp for the day
      - name: status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Latest status recorded that day; 'is_null' if the latest status was NULL; otherwise NULL when status did not change that day
      - name: sprint
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Latest sprint value(s) recorded that day as a comma-separated list; 'is_null' if the latest sprint was NULL; otherwise NULL when sprint did not change that day
      - name: story_points
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Latest 'story points' recorded that day; 'is_null' if the latest value was NULL; otherwise NULL when it did not change that day
      - name: story_point_estimate
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Latest 'story point estimate' recorded that day; 'is_null' if the latest value was NULL; otherwise NULL when it did not change that day
      - name: issue_day_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: MD5 hash of valid_starting_on and issue_id concatenated with no delimiter
        tests:

references.line_text: business_logic: '- Read single-value field changes from intermediate.int_jira__issue_field_history and multiselect field changes from intermediate.int_jira__issue_multiselect_history. - For multiselect changes, aggregate all values per (field_id, field_name, issue_id, updated_at) into one string joined by ", "; duplicates are preserved; NULL inputs are excluded; no ordering is enforced in the concatenation. - Union the aggregated multiselect changes with the single-value changes. - For each issue and field, each change timestamp starts a validity period that lasts until the next change; also derive the calendar date of the start. - Keep only relevant fields: status by field_id (case-insensitive), and sprint, story points, story point estimate by field_name (case-insensitive). - For each issue, field, and calendar date, retain the last change of that day (the highest change timestamp for that day; no tie-breaker beyond timestamp). - Replace a NULL field value with the literal "is_null"; otherwise keep the original text (including any comma-joined multiselect values). - Pivot to columns: status from field_id; sprint, story points, and story point estimate from field_name. Group by issue and date, and carry the week-start of the selected change timestamp. Use max as a pass-through since there is at most one selected value per field per day. - Output includes only dates where at least one relevant field changed for the issue. Unchanged fields on that date remain NULL; fields changed to true NULL appear as "is_null". - Compute issue_day_id as the MD5 of valid_starting_on concatenated with issue_id, with no delimiter.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_jira__project_health_scoring
      description: Multi-dimensional Jira project health scoring with binary risk flags and composite scores
      grain: One row per project_id
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__project
      - staging.stg_jira__issue
      - staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history
      - staging.stg_jira__comment
      - staging.stg_jira__issue_link
      - staging.stg_jira__sprint
      business_logic: 'Build base metrics per project by left-joining issues to projects and aggregating: - total_issues counts all issues; resolved_issues counts issues with a resolution timestamp; open_issues counts issues without one. - avg_resolution_days averages days from creation to resolution over resolved issues; NULL if none. - high_priority_issues counts issues with any priority_id present (proxy for “has priority,” not true severity). - unique_assignees counts distinct non-null assignee IDs. Derive velocity trends per project: - issues_resolved_30d counts issues resolved in the last 30 days; issues_created_30d counts issues created in the last 30 days. - issues_resolved_7d counts issues resolved in the last 7 days. - issues_resolved_prev_30d counts issues resolved 60–30 days before today. Compute quality indicators: - bug_issues counts issues with a non-null issue_type_id; feature_issues uses the same proxy and equals bug_issues. - reopened_issues_count counts all history records whose field value contains “reopen” (case-insensitive). - avg_comments_per_issue averages per-issue comment counts over issues that have at least one comment; NULL if none. Compute team dynamics: - workload_distribution_stddev and max_user_issues are derived from per-assignee issue counts on assigned issues; NULL if no assigned issues. - total_issue_links equals 1 if any project issue participates in any issue link, else 0. - sprints_participated equals the number of distinct sprints in the sprint source and is the same for all projects. Assemble risk flags (0/1): - backlog_risk = 1 if open_issues > 2 × resolved_issues else 0. - velocity_risk = 1 if avg_resolution_days > 30 else 0; NULL avg does not trigger the flag. - quality_risk = 1 if bug_issues > 30% of total_issues else 0. - resource_risk = 1 if unique_assignees < 2 else 0. - throughput_risk = 1 if issues_created_30d > 1.5 × issues_resolved_30d else 0. Compute health scores (each bounded to 0–25): - delivery_health_score starts at 25 and deducts 8 for backlog_risk, 10 for velocity_risk, 7 for throughput_risk. - quality_health_score starts at 25 and deducts 12 for quality_risk, 8 if reopened_issues_count > 10% of total_issues, 5 if avg_comments_per_issue < 1. - team_health_score starts at 25 and deducts 15 for resource_risk, 5 if workload_distribution_stddev > 10, 5 if unique_assignees = 0. - process_health_score starts at 25 and deducts 10 if sprints_participated = 0, 5 if total_issue_links = 0, 10 if high_priority_issues > 50% of total_issues. - velocity_change_percent is the percent change in resolved count vs the prior 30 days; if the prior is 0 then 0; otherwise rounded to one decimal place. Final outputs: - overall_health_score = sum of the four health scores (0–100). - health_grade: A+ (≥90), A (≥80), B (≥70), C (≥60), D (≥50), else F. - primary_risk_factor: dimension with the lowest health score; ties resolve in order Delivery → Quality → Team → Process. - trajectory_status from velocity_change_percent: >20 Accelerating; >5 Improving; >-5 Stable; >-20 Declining; else Critical Decline. - Final result is ordered by overall_health_score descending.'
      columns:
      - name: project_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Project identifier; grouping key with exactly one row per project_id
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: project_key

        description: Project key copied from the project source
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: total_issues

        description: Total number of issues linked to the project
      - name: open_issues

        description: Number of issues without a resolution timestamp
      - name: resolved_issues

        description: Number of issues with a resolution timestamp
      - name: avg_resolution_days
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average days from creation to resolution over resolved issues; NULL if none
      - name: high_priority_issues

        description: Number of issues with a present priority_id (proxy for 'has priority')
      - name: unique_assignees
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct count of non-null assignee IDs across project issues
      - name: issues_resolved_30d
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of issues resolved in the last 30 days based on resolution date
      - name: issues_created_30d
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of issues created in the last 30 days based on creation date
      - name: issues_resolved_7d
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of issues resolved in the last 7 days
      - name: issues_resolved_prev_30d
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of issues resolved 60–30 days before today
      - name: bug_issues
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of issues with a non-null issue_type_id (used as bug proxy)
      - name: feature_issues
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of issues with a non-null issue_type_id (same as bug_issues)
      - name: reopened_issues_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of history records whose field value contains 'reopen' (case-insensitive) across project issues
      - name: avg_comments_per_issue
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average comments per issue over issues with at least one comment; NULL if none
      - name: workload_distribution_stddev
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Standard deviation of issues per assignee within the project; NULL if none
      - name: max_user_issues
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Maximum issues assigned to any single user; NULL if none
      - name: total_issue_links
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: 'Indicator: 1 if any project issue participates in any issue link, else 0'
      - name: sprints_participated
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of distinct sprints in the sprint source (same for all projects)
      - name: backlog_risk
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Flag (0/1): 1 when open_issues > 2 × resolved_issues, else 0'
      - name: velocity_risk
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Flag (0/1): 1 when avg_resolution_days > 30, else 0; NULL avg does not trigger'
      - name: quality_risk
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Flag (0/1): 1 when bug_issues > 30% of total_issues, else 0'
      - name: resource_risk
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Flag (0/1): 1 when unique_assignees < 2, else 0'
      - name: throughput_risk
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'Flag (0/1): 1 when issues_created_30d > 1.5 × issues_resolved_30d, else 0'
      - name: delivery_health_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 0–25 after deducting 8 for backlog_risk, 10 for velocity_risk, 7 for throughput_risk; bounded to 0–25
      - name: quality_health_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 0–25 after deducting 12 for quality_risk, 8 if reopened_issues_count > 10% of total_issues, 5 if avg_comments_per_issue < 1; bounded to 0–25
      - name: team_health_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 0–25 after deducting 15 for resource_risk, 5 if workload_distribution_stddev > 10, 5 if unique_assignees = 0; bounded to 0–25
      - name: process_health_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 0–25 after deducting 10 if sprints_participated = 0, 5 if total_issue_links = 0, 10 if high_priority_issues > 50% of total_issues; bounded to 0–25
      - name: velocity_change_percent
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Percent change in resolved count vs prior 30 days; if prior is 0 then 0; otherwise rounded to 1 decimal
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: overall_health_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Sum of the four health scores, range 0–100
      - name: health_grade
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Letter grade from overall_health_score: A+ (≥90), A (≥80), B (≥70), C (≥60), D (≥50), else F'
      - name: primary_risk_factor
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Dimension with the lowest health score; ties resolve in order Delivery, Quality, Team, Process
      - name: trajectory_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Label from velocity_change_percent: >20 Accelerating; >5 Improving; >-5 Stable; >-20 Declining; else Critical Decline'

business_logic: 'Build base metrics per project by left-joining issues to projects and aggregating: - total_issues counts all issues; resolved_issues counts issues with a resolution timestamp; open_issues counts issues without one. - avg_resolution_days averages days from creation to resolution over resolved issues; NULL if none. - high_priority_issues counts issues with any priority_id present (proxy for “has priority,” not true severity). - unique_assignees counts distinct non-null assignee IDs. Derive velocity trends per project: - issues_resolved_30d counts issues resolved in the last 30 days; issues_created_30d counts issues created in the last 30 days. - issues_resolved_7d counts issues resolved in the last 7 days. - issues_resolved_prev_30d counts issues resolved 60–30 days before today. Compute quality indicators: - bug_issues counts issues with a non-null issue_type_id; feature_issues uses the same proxy and equals bug_issues. - reopened_issues_count counts all history records whose field value contains “reopen” (case-insensitive). - avg_comments_per_issue averages per-issue comment counts over issues that have at least one comment; NULL if none. Compute team dynamics: - workload_distribution_stddev and max_user_issues are derived from per-assignee issue counts on assigned issues; NULL if no assigned issues. - total_issue_links equals 1 if any project issue participates in any issue link, else 0. - sprints_participated equals the number of distinct sprints in the sprint source and is the same for all projects. Assemble risk flags (0/1): - backlog_risk = 1 if open_issues > 2 × resolved_issues else 0. - velocity_risk = 1 if avg_resolution_days > 30 else 0; NULL avg does not trigger the flag. - quality_risk = 1 if bug_issues > 30% of total_issues else 0. - resource_risk = 1 if unique_assignees < 2 else 0. - throughput_risk = 1 if issues_created_30d > 1.5 × issues_resolved_30d else 0. Compute health scores (each bounded to 0–25): - delivery_health_score starts at 25 and deducts 8 for backlog_risk, 10 for velocity_risk, 7 for throughput_risk. - quality_health_score starts at 25 and deducts 12 for quality_risk, 8 if reopened_issues_count > 10% of total_issues, 5 if avg_comments_per_issue < 1. - team_health_score starts at 25 and deducts 15 for resource_risk, 5 if workload_distribution_stddev > 10, 5 if unique_assignees = 0. - process_health_score starts at 25 and deducts 10 if sprints_participated = 0, 5 if total_issue_links = 0, 10 if high_priority_issues > 50% of total_issues. - velocity_change_percent is the percent change in resolved count vs the prior 30 days; if the prior is 0 then 0; otherwise rounded to one decimal place. Final outputs: - overall_health_score = sum of the four health scores (0–100). - health_grade: A+ (≥90), A (≥80), B (≥70), C (≥60), D (≥50), else F. - primary_risk_factor: dimension with the lowest health score; ties resolve in order Delivery → Quality → Team → Process. - trajectory_status from velocity_change_percent: >20 Accelerating; >5 Improving; >-5 Stable; >-20 Declining; else Critical Decline. - Final result is ordered by overall_health_score descending.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_jira__project_metrics
      description: Project-level issue counts and duration metrics (seconds and days) derived from issues; open-age metrics depend on execution time
      grain: One row per project_id
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_jira__issue_join
      business_logic: '- Start from intermediate.int_jira__issue_join and exclude rows with a missing project_id; only projects present in this source appear in the output. - For each project_id: - Counts: - count_closed_issues: number of issues with a resolution timestamp. - count_open_issues: number of issues without a resolution timestamp. - count_open_assigned_issues: number of open issues with an assignee. - count_closed_assigned_issues (internal): number of resolved issues with an assignee. - Sum durations in seconds (non-applicable rows add 0): - Close time: seconds between created_at and resolved_at for resolved issues. - Assigned close time: seconds between first_assigned_at and last_assigned_at for resolved issues where first_assigned_at exists. - Age of currently open: seconds from created_at to the model execution time for open issues. - Age of currently open and assigned: seconds from first_assigned_at to the model execution time for open issues where first_assigned_at exists. - Averages (rounded to the nearest whole second): - avg_close_time_seconds: sum of close time seconds divided by count_closed_issues; if the count is zero, return 0. - avg_assigned_close_time_seconds: sum of assigned close time seconds divided by count_closed_assigned_issues; issues missing first_assigned_at contribute 0 seconds but still count in the denominator; if the count is zero, return 0. - avg_age_currently_open_seconds: sum of open-age seconds divided by count_open_issues; computed relative to the execution time; if the count is zero, return 0. - avg_age_currently_open_assigned_seconds: sum of open-age assigned seconds divided by count_open_assigned_issues; issues missing first_assigned_at contribute 0 seconds but still count in the denominator; computed relative to the execution time; if the count is zero, return 0. - Medians (50th percentile of the applicable seconds, rounded to the nearest whole second): - median_close_time_seconds: among resolved issues; null if there are no applicable durations. - median_age_currently_open_seconds: among open issues measured to the execution time; null if there are no applicable durations. - median_assigned_close_time_seconds: among resolved issues where first_assigned_at and last_assigned_at exist; null if there are no applicable durations. - median_age_currently_open_assigned_seconds: among open issues where first_assigned_at exists, measured to the execution time; null if there are no applicable durations. - Days metrics: convert the corresponding seconds metric to days by dividing by 86400 and rounding to whole days; averages are always non-negative; medians are null when their seconds metric is null.'
      columns:
      - name: project_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Unique project identifier; one row per project
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: count_closed_issues
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Count of issues with a resolution timestamp
        tests:
        - count_closed_issues >= 0
      - name: count_open_issues
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Count of issues without a resolution timestamp
        tests:
        - count_open_issues >= 0
      - name: count_open_assigned_issues
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Count of open issues that have an assignee
        tests:
        - count_open_assigned_issues >= 0
      - name: avg_close_time_seconds
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,0)
        description: Average seconds from creation to resolution across resolved issues, rounded; returns 0 when none
        tests:
        - avg_close_time_seconds >= 0
      - name: avg_assigned_close_time_seconds
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,0)
        description: Average seconds from first to last assignment for resolved issues with an assignee, rounded; issues missing first_assigned_at add 0 seconds; returns 0 when denominator is 0
        tests:
        - avg_assigned_close_time_seconds >= 0
      - name: avg_age_currently_open_seconds
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,0)
        description: Average seconds from creation to the execution time across open issues, rounded; returns 0 when none
        tests:
        - avg_age_currently_open_seconds >= 0
      - name: avg_age_currently_open_assigned_seconds
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,0)
        description: Average seconds from first assignment to the execution time across open issues with an assignee, rounded; issues missing first_assigned_at add 0 seconds; returns 0 when denominator is 0
        tests:
        - avg_age_currently_open_assigned_seconds >= 0
      - name: avg_close_time_days
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,0)
        description: avg_close_time_seconds converted to whole days by dividing by 86400 and rounding
        tests:
        - avg_close_time_days >= 0
      - name: avg_assigned_close_time_days
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,0)
        description: avg_assigned_close_time_seconds converted to whole days by dividing by 86400 and rounding
        tests:
        - avg_assigned_close_time_days >= 0
      - name: avg_age_currently_open_days
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,0)
        description: avg_age_currently_open_seconds converted to whole days by dividing by 86400 and rounding
        tests:
        - avg_age_currently_open_days >= 0
      - name: avg_age_currently_open_assigned_days
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,0)
        description: avg_age_currently_open_assigned_seconds converted to whole days by dividing by 86400 and rounding
        tests:
        - avg_age_currently_open_assigned_days >= 0
      - name: median_close_time_seconds
        data_type: DECIMAL(18,0)

references.name: intermediate.int_jira__issue_join
references.line_text: business_logic: '- Start from intermediate.int_jira__issue_join and exclude rows with a missing project_id; only projects present in this source appear in the output. - For each project_id: - Counts: - count_closed_issues: number of issues with a resolution timestamp. - count_open_issues: number of issues without a resolution timestamp. - count_open_assigned_issues: number of open issues with an assignee. - count_closed_assigned_issues (internal): number of resolved issues with an assignee. - Sum durations in seconds (non-applicable rows add 0): - Close time: seconds between created_at and resolved_at for resolved issues. - Assigned close time: seconds between first_assigned_at and last_assigned_at for resolved issues where first_assigned_at exists. - Age of currently open: seconds from created_at to the model execution time for open issues. - Age of currently open and assigned: seconds from first_assigned_at to the model execution time for open issues where first_assigned_at exists. - Averages (rounded to the nearest whole second): - avg_close_time_seconds: sum of close time seconds divided by count_closed_issues; if the count is zero, return 0. - avg_assigned_close_time_seconds: sum of assigned close time seconds divided by count_closed_assigned_issues; issues missing first_assigned_at contribute 0 seconds but still count in the denominator; if the count is zero, return 0. - avg_age_currently_open_seconds: sum of open-age seconds divided by count_open_issues; computed relative to the execution time; if the count is zero, return 0. - avg_age_currently_open_assigned_seconds: sum of open-age assigned seconds divided by count_open_assigned_issues; issues missing first_assigned_at contribute 0 seconds but still count in the denominator; computed relative to the execution time; if the count is zero, return 0. - Medians (50th percentile of the applicable seconds, rounded to the nearest whole second): - median_close_time_seconds: among resolved issues; null if there are no applicable durations. - median_age_currently_open_seconds: among open issues measured to the execution time; null if there are no applicable durations. - median_assigned_close_time_seconds: among resolved issues where first_assigned_at and last_assigned_at exist; null if there are no applicable durations. - median_age_currently_open_assigned_seconds: among open issues where first_assigned_at exists, measured to the execution time; null if there are no applicable durations. - Days metrics: convert the corresponding seconds metric to days by dividing by 86400 and rounding to whole days; averages are always non-negative; medians are null when their seconds metric is null.'

blocks.original_text:
- name: int_jira__sprint_performance_analytics
      description: Advanced sprint performance analytics with start/end snapshots, burndown, velocity trends, and risk/health classification
      grain: 'One row per sprint_id per generated snapshot (at most two: start and end/complete)'
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_jira__sprint
      - staging.stg_jira__issue
      - staging.stg_jira__issue_field_history
      - staging.stg_jira__field
      business_logic: 'Data assembly: - From staging.stg_jira__sprint, keep sprints with started_at not null. Derive start_date = date(started_at), end_date = date(ended_at), complete_date = date(completed_at). - planned_duration_days = (ended_at - started_at) in days when both exist, else null. actual_duration_days = (completed_at - started_at) in days when both exist (not used later). Sprint issues: - Create sprint_issues by pairing issues with sprints (cross join) and keeping only issue rows where issue.created_at falls between sprint.started_at and coalesce(sprint.completed_at, sprint.ended_at, current_timestamp). Apply a global LIMIT 1000 without ordering, so metrics are based on an arbitrary subset of qualifying rows. - story_points per issue: take the latest active field value whose field name contains “story” and “point”; use the numeric value if the field is numeric or extract the first numeric substring; if unavailable/unparsable, default to 1. - time_spent_seconds and original_estimate_seconds default to 0 when null. Snapshots: - For each sprint, create: - Start snapshot: snapshot_date = start_date, day_number = 1 (always). - End snapshot: only when planned_duration_days > 1; snapshot_date = complete_date, else end_date, else current_date; day_number = planned_duration_days. Metrics per snapshot (group by sprint and snapshot): - total_story_points_committed: sum of story_points across all included issue rows (no de-duplication). - story_points_completed: sum of story_points where issue_resolved_at date is on/before snapshot_date. story_points_remaining: sum of story_points where issue_resolved_at is null or its date is after snapshot_date. - total_issues_committed: count of issue rows. issues_completed: count where resolved on/before snapshot_date. issues_remaining: count where unresolved or resolved after snapshot_date. - total_estimated_hours: sum(original_estimate_seconds)/3600.0. hours_spent_completed: sum(time_spent_seconds) for issues resolved by snapshot_date divided by 3600.0. total_hours_spent: sum(time_spent_seconds)/3600.0. Burndown and indicators (computed within each sprint ordered by day_number): - ideal_story_points_remaining: a linear ideal line from committed at day 1 down to 0 at the end; if planned_duration_days > 0, scale by (1 - (day_number - 1)/planned_duration_days); otherwise keep at committed. - daily_velocity: previous snapshot’s story_points_remaining minus current (null for the first snapshot; may be negative). - completion_ratio: story_points_completed / committed, rounded to 3 decimals; 0 when committed is 0. - timeline_progress_ratio: day_number / planned_duration_days, rounded to 3 decimals when planned_duration_days > 0; otherwise set to 1 (can exceed 1 when planned_duration_days < 1). - scope_change_points and scope_change_issues: change in committed story points and issue count since the previous snapshot (null for the first snapshot). - burndown_variance: story_points_remaining minus ideal_story_points_remaining. - performance_index: completion_ratio divided by timeline_progress_ratio when timeline_progress_ratio > 0; otherwise null. - velocity_trend_3d: moving average of daily_velocity over up to the last three snapshots in the sprint; null when the window has no non-null values. - predicted_completion_day: when daily_velocity > 0 and remaining > 0, forecast as day_number plus (remaining/daily_velocity); otherwise null. Classifications: - sprint_risk_status: Behind Schedule if completion_ratio < timeline_progress_ratio - 0.2; Ahead of Schedule if completion_ratio > timeline_progress_ratio + 0.1; Scope Creep if abs(scope_change_points) > 10% of committed; otherwise On Track. - sprint_health_score (0–100): start at 100; subtract 30 if Behind Schedule; subtract 20 if Scope Creep; subtract 25 if abs(burndown_variance) > 30% of committed; add 10 if Ahead of Schedule; add 15 if performance_index > 1.1; clamp to [0,100]. - velocity_category: High Velocity (>5), Good Velocity (>2), Low Velocity (>0), No Progress (=0), else Negative Velocity. - sprint_phase: Early Phase (timeline_progress_ratio ≤ 0.3), Mid Phase (≤ 0.6), Late Phase (≤ 0.9), else Final Phase. Output is ordered by sprint_id then day_number.'
      columns:
      - name: sprint_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Sprint primary identifier used for grouping and ordering
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: sprint_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Sprint name from staging.stg_jira__sprint
      - name: snapshot_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Snapshot date (start_date; and end/complete/current_date when planned_duration_days > 1)
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: day_number
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Snapshot index: 1 at start; planned_duration_days at end/complete; ordered ascending within each sprint'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - day_number >= 1
      - name: planned_duration_days
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Planned sprint duration in days as (ended_at − started_at)/86400; null if ended_at is null; non-negative when present
        tests:
        - planned_duration_days IS NULL OR planned_duration_days >= 0
      - name: total_story_points_committed
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,3)
        description: Sum of story points for included issue rows; defaults to 1 per issue when the field is missing or unparseable; no de-duplication
        tests:
        - not_null
        - total_story_points_committed >= 0
      - name: story_points_completed
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,3)
        description: Sum of story points for issues resolved on/before snapshot_date
        tests:
        - not_null
        - story_points_completed >= 0
      - name: story_points_remaining
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,3)
        description: Sum of story points for issues unresolved or resolved after snapshot_date
        tests:
        - not_null
        - story_points_remaining >= 0
      - name: total_issues_committed
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of included issue rows within the sprint window
        tests:
        - not_null
        - total_issues_committed >= 0
      - name: issues_completed
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of issues resolved on/before snapshot_date
        tests:
        - not_null
        - issues_completed >= 0
      - name: issues_remaining
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Count of issues unresolved or resolved after snapshot_date
        tests:
        - not_null
        - issues_remaining >= 0
      - name: total_estimated_hours
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total original estimate hours across included issues (seconds summed and divided by 3600.0)
        tests:
        - not_null
        - total_estimated_hours >= 0
      - name: hours_spent_completed
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total hours spent on issues resolved by snapshot_date (seconds summed for those issues and divided by 3600.0)
        tests:
        - not_null
        - hours_spent_completed >= 0
      - name: total_hours_spent
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Total hours spent across included issues (seconds summed and divided by 3600.0)
        tests:
        - not_null
        - total_hours_spent >= 0
      - name: ideal_story_points_remaining
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Ideal remaining story points based on a straight-line burndown from committed at day 1 to 0 at the end; if no planned duration, equals committed
        tests:
        - not_null
        - ideal_story_points_remaining >= 0
      - name: daily_velocity
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,3)
        description: Change in story_points_remaining since the previous snapshot; null for the first snapshot; may be negative
      - name: completion_ratio
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Rounded to 3 decimals: story_points_completed divided by committed; 0 when committed is 0; range [0,1]'
        tests:
        - completion_ratio >= 0 AND completion_ratio <= 1
      - name: timeline_progress_ratio
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Rounded to 3 decimals: day_number divided by planned_duration_days when planned_duration_days > 0, else 1; may exceed 1 when planned_duration_days < 1'
        tests:
        - timeline_progress_ratio >= 0
      - name: scope_change_points
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,3)
        description: Change in committed story points since the previous snapshot; null for the first snapshot; may be positive or negative
      - name: scope_change_issues
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Change in committed issue count since the previous snapshot; null for the first snapshot; may be positive or negative
      - name: burndown_variance
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Difference between actual remaining and ideal remaining story points; positive means behind ideal, negative means ahead
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: performance_index
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Ratio of completion to timeline progress when progress is > 0; null otherwise; values > 1 indicate ahead of timeline
      - name: velocity_trend_3d
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Moving average of daily_velocity over up to the last three snapshots within the sprint; null when the window has no non-null values
      - name: predicted_completion_day
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Forecasted completion snapshot index: current day_number plus remaining divided by daily_velocity when both positive; otherwise null'
        tests:
        - predicted_completion_day IS NULL OR predicted_completion_day > day_number
      - name: sprint_risk_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Risk label based on completion vs timeline thresholds and scope change: Behind/Ahead/Scope Creep/On Track'
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: sprint_health_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Score from 0 to 100 using penalties for risk and variance and bonuses for positive indicators, clamped to the range
        tests:
        - not_null
        - sprint_health_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100

references.name: staging.stg_jira__sprint
references.line_text: business_logic: 'Data assembly: - From staging.stg_jira__sprint, keep sprints with started_at not null. Derive start_date = date(started_at), end_date = date(ended_at), complete_date = date(completed_at). - planned_duration_days = (ended_at - started_at) in days when both exist, else null. actual_duration_days = (completed_at - started_at) in days when both exist (not used later). Sprint issues: - Create sprint_issues by pairing issues with sprints (cross join) and keeping only issue rows where issue.created_at falls between sprint.started_at and coalesce(sprint.completed_at, sprint.ended_at, current_timestamp). Apply a global LIMIT 1000 without ordering, so metrics are based on an arbitrary subset of qualifying rows. - story_points per issue: take the latest active field value whose field name contains “story” and “point”; use the numeric value if the field is numeric or extract the first numeric substring; if unavailable/unparsable, default to 1. - time_spent_seconds and original_estimate_seconds default to 0 when null. Snapshots: - For each sprint, create: - Start snapshot: snapshot_date = start_date, day_number = 1 (always). - End snapshot: only when planned_duration_days > 1; snapshot_date = complete_date, else end_date, else current_date; day_number = planned_duration_days. Metrics per snapshot (group by sprint and snapshot): - total_story_points_committed: sum of story_points across all included issue rows (no de-duplication). - story_points_completed: sum of story_points where issue_resolved_at date is on/before snapshot_date. story_points_remaining: sum of story_points where issue_resolved_at is null or its date is after snapshot_date. - total_issues_committed: count of issue rows. issues_completed: count where resolved on/before snapshot_date. issues_remaining: count where unresolved or resolved after snapshot_date. - total_estimated_hours: sum(original_estimate_seconds)/3600.0. hours_spent_completed: sum(time_spent_seconds) for issues resolved by snapshot_date divided by 3600.0. total_hours_spent: sum(time_spent_seconds)/3600.0. Burndown and indicators (computed within each sprint ordered by day_number): - ideal_story_points_remaining: a linear ideal line from committed at day 1 down to 0 at the end; if planned_duration_days > 0, scale by (1 - (day_number - 1)/planned_duration_days); otherwise keep at committed. - daily_velocity: previous snapshot’s story_points_remaining minus current (null for the first snapshot; may be negative). - completion_ratio: story_points_completed / committed, rounded to 3 decimals; 0 when committed is 0. - timeline_progress_ratio: day_number / planned_duration_days, rounded to 3 decimals when planned_duration_days > 0; otherwise set to 1 (can exceed 1 when planned_duration_days < 1). - scope_change_points and scope_change_issues: change in committed story points and issue count since the previous snapshot (null for the first snapshot). - burndown_variance: story_points_remaining minus ideal_story_points_remaining. - performance_index: completion_ratio divided by timeline_progress_ratio when timeline_progress_ratio > 0; otherwise null. - velocity_trend_3d: moving average of daily_velocity over up to the last three snapshots in the sprint; null when the window has no non-null values. - predicted_completion_day: when daily_velocity > 0 and remaining > 0, forecast as day_number plus (remaining/daily_velocity); otherwise null. Classifications: - sprint_risk_status: Behind Schedule if completion_ratio < timeline_progress_ratio - 0.2; Ahead of Schedule if completion_ratio > timeline_progress_ratio + 0.1; Scope Creep if abs(scope_change_points) > 10% of committed; otherwise On Track. - sprint_health_score (0–100): start at 100; subtract 30 if Behind Schedule; subtract 20 if Scope Creep; subtract 25 if abs(burndown_variance) > 30% of committed; add 10 if Ahead of Schedule; add 15 if performance_index > 1.1; clamp to [0,100]. - velocity_category: High Velocity (>5), Good Velocity (>2), Low Velocity (>0), No Progress (=0), else Negative Velocity. - sprint_phase: Early Phase (timeline_progress_ratio ≤ 0.3), Mid Phase (≤ 0.6), Late Phase (≤ 0.9), else Final Phase. Output is ordered by sprint_id then day_number.'

business_logic: 'Data assembly: - From staging.stg_jira__sprint, keep sprints with started_at not null. Derive start_date = date(started_at), end_date = date(ended_at), complete_date = date(completed_at). - planned_duration_days = (ended_at - started_at) in days when both exist, else null. actual_duration_days = (completed_at - started_at) in days when both exist (not used later). Sprint issues: - Create sprint_issues by pairing issues with sprints (cross join) and keeping only issue rows where issue.created_at falls between sprint.started_at and coalesce(sprint.completed_at, sprint.ended_at, current_timestamp). Apply a global LIMIT 1000 without ordering, so metrics are based on an arbitrary subset of qualifying rows. - story_points per issue: take the latest active field value whose field name contains “story” and “point”; use the numeric value if the field is numeric or extract the first numeric substring; if unavailable/unparsable, default to 1. - time_spent_seconds and original_estimate_seconds default to 0 when null. Snapshots: - For each sprint, create: - Start snapshot: snapshot_date = start_date, day_number = 1 (always). - End snapshot: only when planned_duration_days > 1; snapshot_date = complete_date, else end_date, else current_date; day_number = planned_duration_days. Metrics per snapshot (group by sprint and snapshot): - total_story_points_committed: sum of story_points across all included issue rows (no de-duplication). - story_points_completed: sum of story_points where issue_resolved_at date is on/before snapshot_date. story_points_remaining: sum of story_points where issue_resolved_at is null or its date is after snapshot_date. - total_issues_committed: count of issue rows. issues_completed: count where resolved on/before snapshot_date. issues_remaining: count where unresolved or resolved after snapshot_date. - total_estimated_hours: sum(original_estimate_seconds)/3600.0. hours_spent_completed: sum(time_spent_seconds) for issues resolved by snapshot_date divided by 3600.0. total_hours_spent: sum(time_spent_seconds)/3600.0. Burndown and indicators (computed within each sprint ordered by day_number): - ideal_story_points_remaining: a linear ideal line from committed at day 1 down to 0 at the end; if planned_duration_days > 0, scale by (1 - (day_number - 1)/planned_duration_days); otherwise keep at committed. - daily_velocity: previous snapshot’s story_points_remaining minus current (null for the first snapshot; may be negative). - completion_ratio: story_points_completed / committed, rounded to 3 decimals; 0 when committed is 0. - timeline_progress_ratio: day_number / planned_duration_days, rounded to 3 decimals when planned_duration_days > 0; otherwise set to 1 (can exceed 1 when planned_duration_days < 1). - scope_change_points and scope_change_issues: change in committed story points and issue count since the previous snapshot (null for the first snapshot). - burndown_variance: story_points_remaining minus ideal_story_points_remaining. - performance_index: completion_ratio divided by timeline_progress_ratio when timeline_progress_ratio > 0; otherwise null. - velocity_trend_3d: moving average of daily_velocity over up to the last three snapshots in the sprint; null when the window has no non-null values. - predicted_completion_day: when daily_velocity > 0 and remaining > 0, forecast as day_number plus (remaining/daily_velocity); otherwise null. Classifications: - sprint_risk_status: Behind Schedule if completion_ratio < timeline_progress_ratio - 0.2; Ahead of Schedule if completion_ratio > timeline_progress_ratio + 0.1; Scope Creep if abs(scope_change_points) > 10% of committed; otherwise On Track. - sprint_health_score (0–100): start at 100; subtract 30 if Behind Schedule; subtract 20 if Scope Creep; subtract 25 if abs(burndown_variance) > 30% of committed; add 10 if Ahead of Schedule; add 15 if performance_index > 1.1; clamp to [0,100]. - velocity_category: High Velocity (>5), Good Velocity (>2), Low Velocity (>0), No Progress (=0), else Negative Velocity. - sprint_phase: Early Phase (timeline_progress_ratio ≤ 0.3), Mid Phase (≤ 0.6), Late Phase (≤ 0.9), else Final Phase. Output is ordered by sprint_id then day_number.'
